Exam objectives are paraphrased from the vendors' public objective documents; this course maps its own modules (IL27-M01..M24) to those public descriptions. No vendor text is reproduced.

domains.objectives: Laptop and tablet hardware, displays, accessories and ports; mobile OS configuration, network connectivity, synchronization, and mobile security practices.
domains.note: Hardware identification and mobile config anchored in M01.

domains.objectives: Cable types and connectors, common TCP/UDP ports and protocols, wireless standards, SOHO router setup, and core network services (DNS, DHCP).
domains.note: Core networking in M03; deepened by IL27-M07 in the Network+ track.

domains.objectives: Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, storage devices, power supplies, cooling, display technologies, printers, and custom PC builds.
domains.note: Component-level knowledge built hands-on in M02 labs.

domains.objectives: Hypervisor concepts, VM configuration basics, cloud models and deployment types, and resource requirements for cloud services.
domains.note: Concepts in M03; hands-on VM management deepened in M17 (AZ-800 track).

domains.objectives: Structured troubleshooting methodology, common hardware and network symptoms, diagnostic tools, and resolution steps.
domains.note: The triage methodology taught in M04 is reused across every later track.

domains.objectives: Windows editions and features, install/upgrade procedures, command-line tools, Control Panel utilities, and OS-level networking configuration.
domains.note: OS administration fundamentals in M05; server editions in M16.

domains.objectives: Physical and logical security concepts, threat types, Windows security settings, workstation best practices, and access control basics.
domains.note: Feeds directly into the Security+ track (M11-M14).

domains.objectives: PC and mobile OS failure symptoms, malware identification and removal steps, and application-level troubleshooting.
domains.note: Malware-removal workflow drilled in M06; triage method from M04.

domains.objectives: Safety and environmental controls, professionalism and communication, documentation, incident response basics, and change management.
domains.note: Ticketing and documentation artifacts produced in M06 become portfolio items.

readinessChecklist: Complete IL27-M01 through M06 with all labs and drills green
Identify hardware components and cable/connector types on sight
Run the M04 triage methodology end-to-end on 5 practice scenarios
Configure Windows networking (IP, DNS, shares, printers) without notes
Execute the malware-removal workflow from M06 from memory
Score 80%+ twice on gate-aplus (50 questions, 90 minutes)

readinessDashboard.title: IL-27 Certification Readiness Dashboard
readinessDashboard.framing: Independent readiness tracking for IL-27. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by CompTIA, Microsoft, or ThreatLocker.
readinessDashboard.concept: For each of the 6 certifications, the dashboard shows a readiness percentage computed from required-module completion and best practice-gate score. Tick off modules and record gate scores as you study; the dashboard recomputes automatically so you can see at a glance which certifications you are prepared to sit for.
howToUse: Work modules in sequence; mark a module complete only when its labs and drills are green.
Sit a practice gate only when the dashboard row reads at least NEARLY READY (70%).
Record each gate score; the dashboard uses your BEST score for the 40% component.
Book the real vendor exam only when the row reads READY TO SIT (>=85%) — score >=80% on the gate twice, as the readiness rule requires.
